candidates.topic: The Mary Celeste — Ghost Ship Mystery
candidates.teaser: A ship found perfectly intact in the middle of the ocean — hot food still on the table, no crew, no bodies, no answers.
candidates.video_title: A Ship Found Drifting — No Crew, No Clue
candidates.video_description: In 1872, the Mary Celeste was discovered adrift in the Atlantic with everything untouched — cargo, food, valuables — yet every single person aboard had vanished. No distress signal was ever sent. No explanation has ever been confirmed.
candidates.script: A ship was found in the middle of the Atlantic — hot food still on the table, cargo untouched, valuables on board. Not a single person was there. No lifeboats missing, no blood, no SOS. The Mary Celeste had 10 people on it when it left New York in 1872. It arrived in Portugal perfectly intact. 150 years later, no one has ever explained where they went.

candidates.teaser: If you've ever scared a crow, there's a real chance it told its friends — and they're still watching you.
candidates.video_title: Crows Never Forget a Face — And They Tell Others
candidates.video_description: Crows can recognize individual human faces and hold grudges for years. Researchers at the University of Washington proved this by wearing masks — crows that were caught scolded that specific mask for over five years, even teaching younger crows to do the same.
candidates.script: If you've ever messed with a crow, it remembered your face. Researchers at the University of Washington wore a specific mask while catching crows. Five years later, those same crows — and their offspring — still dive-bombed anyone wearing that mask. They taught the grudge to the next generation. Crows have been observed holding funerals for their dead and using tools. They may be smarter than most animals you respect.

candidates.teaser: For a decade, a mysterious signal jammed radios across the entire world — and governments refused to explain what it was.
candidates.video_title: A Signal Jammed Every Radio on Earth for 10 Years
candidates.video_description: From 1976 to 1989, a loud repetitive signal known as the Soviet Woodpecker interrupted radio broadcasts globally. It was so powerful and widespread that people thought it was mind control. It turned out to be something almost equally unsettling.
candidates.script: Starting in 1976, a loud tapping signal began jamming radios, TVs, and communications across the entire world simultaneously. It happened every day for 13 years. Governments denied its existence. Civilians thought it was mind control. It was actually a Soviet radar system called Duga — built to detect a US nuclear launch. It was so powerful it bounced signals off the ionosphere. The transmitter still stands abandoned in Chernobyl's exclusion zone.

candidates.teaser: The moment cold water touches your face, your body starts doing something your brain didn't ask for — and it might be the reason some people survive the impossible.
candidates.video_title: Cold Water on Your Face Triggers a Hidden Survival Mode
candidates.video_description: The mammalian diving reflex is an involuntary response that slows your heart rate by up to 50% the instant cold water touches your face. It redirects blood to vital organs and has been credited with saving people who were submerged for over 40 minutes.
candidates.script: Splash cold water on your face right now and your heart rate drops by up to 50% — automatically, instantly, without your brain deciding anything. It's called the mammalian diving reflex, and every human is born with it. It floods blood to your heart and brain, shuts down everything else, and buys you time. It's the reason people have been pulled from frozen lakes after 40 minutes underwater — and survived. Your body is still half aquatic.

candidates.teaser: The moment you learn something new, you start seeing it absolutely everywhere — and there's a disturbing reason your brain does this.
candidates.video_title: Why You See Things Everywhere After Learning About Them
candidates.video_description: The Baader-Meinhof phenomenon, or frequency illusion, is a cognitive bias where something you just noticed suddenly seems to appear constantly. It's not coincidence — your brain is actively filtering reality based on what it decided matters.
candidates.script: You learn a new word, and suddenly you hear it three times that same day. You buy a red car, and now red cars are everywhere. This isn't coincidence — it's your brain lying to you. It's called the Baader-Meinhof phenomenon. Your brain filters out most of reality to save energy. The moment something gets tagged as important, it stops hiding it. Which means the world you see every day is curated by your own past decisions. What else is it hiding?
